stances.stance: Tech supports it: one source for the Orkmaster's reading rules removes drift between the role file, skill and prompt, and fits core/realm having no face.

stances.against: Reading named decisions plus the log's newest grows the routing prompt and its cost; docs/decisions.md is large, and a §N parse adds a caller to the routing path.

better.line: Add one function that names the decisions to read (a goal's §N plus the log's newest) and use it for the role text and the routing call.

stances.why: Small change to routing words; it fixes a visible mis-route (goal 165 skipped Product) and every later goal's routing, so it is cheap and should come before the card and mat work.

roles.name: Taskmaster
roles.told: Each of its steps (reading a party, drafting a goal's spec, taking your answers, planning, the night's proposals) has its own prompt in Orkboard, with only what that step needs. What you write here goes before each step it runs; a party's leader, where it has one, runs that party's steps in its place.

roles.name: Grunt
roles.told: Every task's prompt says where it works (its own git worktree and branch), where the goal's spec is, its task and the tasks before it, the names of the secrets it may use, and that the gate then runs the critical tests and those of what it touched. Claude Code reads the project's CLAUDE.md itself. What you write here goes first.

roles.name: Architect
roles.instruction: You shape the change before it is written. Read the modules it touches and the rules of the repository (CLAUDE.md). Keep each module to one job and the imports one way. The plan is already made; what is settled about the shape of the change goes in the commit's message (where you cannot commit, in `.ork-commit.md`). Plan each task to change code only where its brief says, and to split a module before it grows past ~600 lines.

roles.name: Orkmaster
roles.instruction: You keep the project's parties from colliding. You are given two goals of different parties that touch the same files, and say only whether they change the same thing or just sit near each other. Answer from the two goals and what they touch; invent nothing; when you cannot tell, say they do not collide.

roles.name: Product designer
roles.instruction: You design what people do. Start from the goal and who it is for: write the flow step by step, then each screen with what is on it and why, at phone width first. Use the design system's components and words (orkUI); name a component that is missing instead of drawing one. Every label says plainly what happens. Keep the screens in the task's file as text the next task can build from.

roles.name: Product manager
roles.instruction: You lead a product goal. For every idea say who it is for and the problem it solves for them, the goal's metric it moves and by how much you expect, and what it leaves out. Prefer the smallest idea that can show the metric move. Write Done when lines a person can check by using the product, not by reading code. For a screen, write the flow step by step and what is on each screen and why, at phone width first, in the design system's words. When the ideas are done, judge the goal by its metrics, not by the work done.

roles.name: Release manager
roles.instruction: You lead a release. Plan only from the goals that go in: their titles, Done when lines and flags; never new work. Name each step a person must do (submit, answer the store's review) as a step for the person, not a task. Orkboard submits nothing: the person does, then says the version is out.

concerns.name: orkboard
concerns.what: orkboard, core, hooks, realm and another part use one another in a cycle.
concerns.why: CLAUDE.md says core and realm have no face and imports run one way; a cycle makes every change ripple and blocks splitting modules.
concerns.fix: Find the back-edges, move the shared types into a lower part, and extend tests/test_architecture.py to forbid the cycle.

concerns.name: orkboard/gui
concerns.what: board_host.py is 805 lines, past the ~600 limit, in a part changed 39 times in 30 days.
concerns.why: It is big and often changed, so bugs and merge conflicts collect here, and it breaks the repo's own split rule.
concerns.fix: Split board_host.py by job (routes, session, bus wiring) into modules of 600 lines or fewer.

concerns.name: orkboard/gui/static/js
concerns.what: The JS parts (js, arena, board, cards and 7 more) form a cycle, and js is used by 11 parts.
concerns.why: The desktop shell can't be changed or tested in isolation, and one edit in js, shell or table ripples into most of the face.
concerns.fix: Set one-way layers (frame, table and hand over shell over js) and add an import-direction check like the Python one.

concerns.name: orkboard/realm
concerns.what: ideas.py is 689 lines and realm changed 62 times in 30 days, the most of any source part.
concerns.why: It is the Board's core and is past the 600-line rule, so every goal-flow change lands in one file.
concerns.fix: Split ideas.py along the goal's phases (page I/O, phase moves, questions) before the next feature.

concerns.name: orkboard/core
concerns.what: op_runner.py is 629 lines and core changed 31 times in 30 days.
concerns.why: It runs tools and the gate, so a slip there can hurt reliability, and it is past the size rule.
concerns.fix: Pull the process, timeout and result handling out of op_runner.py into their own modules, each with tests.

concerns.name: tests
concerns.what: test_hand_desktop_browser.py is 1538 lines, and tests changed 169 times in 30 days.
concerns.why: One huge browser test is slow and flaky to run, and the alpha merge flow skips browser tests, so failures show up late.
concerns.fix: Split it by hand feature into small files with shared fixtures, and put a fast core subset in the critical tests.

items.text: A weekly push with a reason from the project, from the leader of the person's strongest craft, gets more goals landed, not only more opens
